intro.title: Accordion
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple accordion component, a UI element that allows users to expand and collapse sections of content. You will learn how to manage component state to track which accordion item is currently open. The core concept involves using React's useState hook to handle this interactive state. You will implement this using TypeScript in a .tsx file, ensuring type safety for your state variables. By the end, you'll have a functional accordion that toggles content visibility with a click.
intro.usecase: Accordions are essential UI components in modern web applications where space optimization and organized content presentation are crucial. You'll find them in FAQ sections on e-commerce sites, where they collapse lengthy answers until users click questions. They're also widely used in dashboard interfaces to toggle between different data panels, in mobile navigation menus that expand categories, and in complex forms where optional fields or advanced settings are hidden by default. As a React developer, implementing reusable accordion components helps create clean, intuitive interfaces that manage information density effectively.
